channel.title: Smart Cities Dive - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Smart Cities Dive (smartcitiesdive.com)

item.title: How housing policy reform drove down rents in Austin, Texas
item.description: Removing regulatory barriers and subsidizing affordable housing helped clear the way for 120,000 new homes in the city between 2015 and 2024, according to Pew.

item.title: How the new NYC schools chief plans to improve rigor and equity
item.description: Kamar Samuels stresses partnerships with elected officials and community-based organizations to manage school mergers and closures.

item.title: Cities sue EPA over endangerment finding repeal
item.description: A dozen cities and counties join states in challenging EPA’s rescission of a cornerstone climate rule, which leaves cities “to bear the costs of hotter summers, dirtier air, and extreme weather,” Denver’s mayor said.

item.title: Idaho updates grant-management system with cloud-based platform
item.description: The modernization project consolidated multiple grant processes across state agencies into one system. It’s already saving time.

item.title: Uber to buy up to 50,000 robotaxis from Rivian by 2030
item.description: The agreement includes an upfront purchase of 10,000 Rivian vehicles, with an option for 40,000 more. Uber previously committed to buy up to 20,000 autonomous vehicles from Lucid.

item.title: City officials urge federal grant application reform
item.description: The “mind-numbing” grant application process could be improved through preparation, intention and building connections, city leaders said during a National League of Cities panel.

item.title: NYC reinvigorates push for ADUs
item.description: The city launched a dedicated website and is restarting a program to offer up to $395,000 to help qualifying homeowners build an ancillary dwelling unit.

item.title: To make housing more affordable, invest in infrastructure
item.description: Homes need roads, water systems and power to serve them. A good start is renewing the federal surface transportation funding set to expire in September, writes a building materials executive.

item.title: New York’s MTA plans to replace more than a third of its subway fleet
item.description: “We are in the midst of a public transit renaissance in New York,” said Gov. Kathy Hochul.

item.title: Cities struggle to meet drinking water PFAS standards by EPA deadline
item.description: Communities are grappling with how to fund removing PFAS “forever chemicals” from their water supplies, experts said during a National League of Cities panel.

item.title: 43% of public sector employees use AI at least a few times a year, Gallup finds
item.description: Less than 40% of the public sector employees surveyed said their organization has a clear AI strategy, according to a recent poll.

item.title: How smart transit bus doors could improve passenger safety
item.description: An artificial intelligence system from Wabtec can detect when riders enter or exit a bus.

item.title: Trump housing order could mean new barriers to federal funding for cities
item.description: Local governments may need to ease zoning and environmental rules to stay eligible for federal support, an attorney says.

item.title: Office-to-housing conversion initiatives proliferate in California
item.description: State policymakers have been pursuing policy changes that remove barriers to converting older commercial buildings into housing, with mixed success.

item.title: Detroit to dedicate 100% of city-owned commercial property sales proceeds to affordable housing fund
item.description: The measure is expected to generate $4 million annually for affordable housing development and preservation.
